extracted.intended_audience: public relations professionals, corporate communicators, organizational leaders, and communications students
extracted.subtask_description: High-level ethical and practical principles for corporate public relations and communications that guide how organizations should speak, act, listen, manage crises, and treat employees as ambassadors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tell the truth.
rubrics_metrics.description: Let the public know what’s happening with honest and good intention; provide an ethically accurate picture of the enterprise’s character, values, ideals and actions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prove it with action.
rubrics_metrics.description: Public perception of an enterprise is determined 90 percent by what it does and 10 percent by what it says.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that words must be backed by consistent behavior; actions are the primary driver of reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Listen to stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.description: To serve the enterprise well, understand what the public wants and needs and advocate for engagement with all stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Keep top decision makers and other employees informed about stakeholder reaction to the enterprise’s products, policies and practices. To listen effectively, engage a diverse range of stakeholders through inclusive dialogue.

rubrics_metrics.name: Manage for tomorrow.
rubrics_metrics.description: Anticipate public reaction and eliminate practices that create difficulties. Generate goodwill.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Frame PR as forward-looking risk management: identify potential public responses and remove or change practices that will cause future problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conduct public relations as if the whole enterprise depends on it.
rubrics_metrics.description: No strategy should be implemented without considering its impact on stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat public relations as a management and policymaking function that encourages decision making, policies and actions to consider stakeholders' diverse views, values, experience, expectations and aspirations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Realize an enterprise's true character is expressed by its people.
rubrics_metrics.description: The strongest opinions—good or bad—about an enterprise are shaped by the words and deeds of an increasingly diverse workforce.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Every employee—active or retired—is involved with public relations. Corporate communications should advocate for respect, diversity and inclusion and support employees’ capability and desire to be honest, knowledgeable ambassadors to customers, friends, shareowners and public officials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remain calm, patient and good-humored.
rubrics_metrics.description: Lay the groundwork for public relations successes with consistent and reasoned attention to information and stakeholders.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When a crisis arises, remember that cool heads communicate best; emphasize patience, composure and measured responses.
